summary: Central runtime configuration. At import time it loads an optional `.env` file, reads every environment variable the platform understands (API key, database URL, CORS origins, demo mode, rate limit, OpenAI settings, host and port) into one immutable `settings` object, and defines the project's folder paths. Every other module imports `settings`, `WEB_DIR` or `DATA_DIR` from here instead of reading the environment itself.

notes.text: Docstring title: this module is the single home of runtime configuration.

States the design rule: each setting is read once, here, from environment variables, optionally pre-loaded from a `.env` file. Everything else imports `settings`, so there is exactly one place listing every knob and its default (`.env.example` documents them for users).
Postponed evaluation of annotations: type hints are stored as strings rather than evaluated at import time. It is a standard header across the codebase.
`os` provides `os.getenv(name, default)`, which returns an environment variable's value as a string, or the default when the variable is not set.
`dataclass` generates `__init__`, `__repr__` and equality methods for a class that is essentially a bundle of typed fields.
`Path` (from `pathlib`) treats filesystem paths as objects; the `/` operator joins segments correctly on both Windows and Linux.
`load_dotenv` comes from the `python-dotenv` package (listed in `requirements.txt`) and copies `KEY=value` lines from a file into the process environment.

Finds the project root from this file's own location: `__file__` is the path of `config.py`, `.resolve()` makes it absolute, and two `.parent` steps climb from `iip/config.py` to the folder that contains `iip/`. Anchoring on `__file__` keeps paths correct whichever directory you launch from.

Derived folders: `WEB_DIR` holds the frontend that `app.py` serves (the `index.html` page and the `/static` mount), and `DATA_DIR` is where the default SQLite file lives (`database.py` creates the folder if needed).

Loads `.env` from the project root into `os.environ` before `load_settings()` runs below. python-dotenv does not override variables that are already set, so a real environment variable beats the file, and a missing `.env` is silently skipped; `tests/conftest.py` relies on this by setting its test values before importing `iip`.

`_flag` reads a variable as a boolean (the leading underscore marks it as private to this module). If the variable is missing, `str(default)` supplies `"True"` or `"False"`; the value is then trimmed and lower-cased, and only `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` count as true, so anything else (`false`, `0`, a typo) means false.

`_csv` turns a comma-separated variable into a tuple of trimmed, non-empty items, so `"a, b,,c"` becomes `("a", "b", "c")`. It returns a tuple rather than a list because tuples are immutable, matching the frozen dataclass below.
`@dataclass(frozen=True)` makes `Settings` an immutable record: assigning to a field after creation raises `FrozenInstanceError`, so no code can change the configuration at runtime by accident.

`api_key` is the shared secret that write endpoints (POST/PATCH) expect in the `X-API-Key` header, checked in `routes/deps.py`. `database_url` is a SQLAlchemy connection URL telling `database.py` which database to open.

`cors_origins` lists the web origins allowed to call the API from a browser page on another site (CORS, enforced by middleware in `app.py`). `demo_mode` controls whether `app.py` injects the API key into the dashboard page, and `rate_limit_per_minute` sizes the per-client token bucket guarding write endpoints and `/ai/ask`.

OpenAI settings used by `analyst.py`. `openai_api_key` is `str | None` because `None` means "no key: use the deterministic analyst", and the model name plus base URL allow any OpenAI-compatible service.
`host` and `port` are the default bind address that `__main__.py` passes to uvicorn.
`load_settings()` reads the environment and returns one `Settings` instance.

Builds the object with keyword arguments, one field per line, each pairing an environment variable with its fallback. `api_key` falls back to `demo-key-change-me`, a value that announces it must be replaced for anything beyond a laptop demo.
`IIP_DB_URL`, defaulting to a SQLite URL that points at `data/iip.db` by absolute path (`sqlite:///` is followed by the file path). The tests swap in a temporary database through this variable.
`IIP_CORS_ORIGINS`, parsed by `_csv`; by default only the dashboard's own origins on port 8000 are allowed.
`IIP_DEMO_MODE`, parsed by `_flag` and on by default, so the demo works without typing a key.
`IIP_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, default 240. `int()` raises an error at start-up if the value is not a number, so a misconfiguration fails fast instead of surfacing later.
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, with `or None` turning an empty string into `None`. That matters because `.env.example` ships the line `OPENAI_API_KEY=` with no value, which must count as "not configured".
`OPENAI_MODEL`, defaulting to `gpt-4o-mini`.
`OPENAI_BASE_URL`; `.rstrip("/")` removes any trailing slash so `analyst.py` can append `/chat/completions` without producing a double slash.
`IIP_HOST`, defaulting to `127.0.0.1` (loopback: reachable only from this machine). The `Dockerfile` sets it to `0.0.0.0` so the server listens on all network interfaces inside the container.

`PORT` breaks the `IIP_` naming pattern: it is the conventional variable many hosting platforms set to tell an app which port to bind, so honouring it lets the app run there unchanged. It defaults to 8000, and the `)` closes the `Settings(...)` call.

Creates the module-level singleton once, the first time `iip.config` is imported; every other module does `from .config import settings`. Because values are read at import time, changing an environment variable afterwards has no effect until the process restarts.
